record.paper_title: Non-Supersymmetric (but) Extreme Black Holes, Scalar Hair and Other Open Problems
record.context_brief: Deriving Bogomol'nyi bounds with primary scalar hair
record.original_question: Can generalized Bogomol'nyi bounds in supergravity be rigorously derived so that they include primary scalar charges, using a Nester construction based on the fermionic supersymmetry transformation laws, while allowing boundary conditions broad enough to include the naked singularities that primary scalar hair appears to imply?

evidence.quote: Scalar charges, not being protected by a gauge symmetry, are not conserved charges. For minimally-coupled scalars the standard no-hair theorems apply and any non-vanishing value implies the presence of naked singularities. The prototype of this kind of singular solution with non-trivial scalar hair (called primary hair) is the one given in Refs. [27] for the theory with a massless scalar ϕ and action
We are going to argue, however, that primary scalar hair should be incorporated into the generalized B bounds.

Although our reasoning is completely clear when we look on specific solutions one should be able to derive B bounds including primary scalar charges using a Nester construction based on the SUSY transformation laws of the fermions of the supergravity theory under consideration. To be able to do this one has to be able to manage more general boundary conditions including the seemingly unavoidable naked singularities that primary hair implies.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a four-dimensional supergravity theory containing gravity, gauge fields, and scalar fields, with known fermionic supersymmetry transformation laws δψ for the gravitino and δχ for the spin-1/2 fields. The standard Witten–Nester construction associates to a spinor field ε satisfying suitable asymptotic conditions a 2-form whose integral over a sphere at spatial infinity gives the ADM mass minus a sum of central-charge contributions (electric, magnetic, etc.), and whose exterior derivative is a manifestly non-negative bulk quadratic form in the supersymmetry variations δψ and δχ. This yields generalized Bogomol'nyi (BPS) bounds of the schematic form

   M ≥ F(Q_e, Q_m, …),

with saturation when ε is a Killing spinor.

A scalar field φ that is not protected by a gauge symmetry can carry a non-conserved "primary scalar charge" Σ defined by the asymptotic expansion φ = φ_∞ + Σ/r + O(1/r²). In known examples (e.g. the massless dilaton coupled to Einstein–Maxwell with action ∫(R − 2(∂φ)² − e^{−2aφ}F²) √(−g) d⁴x), configurations carrying non-trivial Σ independent of the electric/magnetic charges generically possess naked singularities and violate the standard no-hair theorems.

Problem. Formulate and rigorously prove a generalized Bogomol'nyi bound of the form

   M ≥ G(Q_e, Q_m, Σ, …)

in such a supergravity theory, derived via a Nester-type 2-form constructed from the fermionic SUSY transformation laws, in which the primary scalar charge Σ appears explicitly on the right-hand side. The derivation must allow boundary conditions on the spinor ε and on the spacetime fields that are sufficiently general to admit the naked singularities implied by non-trivial primary scalar hair, while still yielding a positive-semidefinite bulk integrand and a well-defined boundary integral at infinity. Determine the precise function G and characterize the configurations saturating the bound.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search returned related works (e.g. Bogomol'nyi bounds in Einstein–Maxwell–dilaton gravity, arXiv:1011.0261, and earlier Nester-type constructions in supergravity), but no source was found that rigorously derives generalized Bogomol'nyi bounds incorporating primary scalar charges via a Nester construction with boundary conditions permitting the naked singularities required by primary scalar hair. The current status of this specific problem could not be definitively verified.

status_evidence.title: On the Bogomol'nyi bound in Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton gravity
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses Bogomol'nyi-type bounds in Einstein-Maxwell-dilaton gravity, a setting where primary scalar (dilaton) charges arise.
status_evidence.claim: Related work addresses BPS bounds with dilaton charges but not via a fully general Nester construction admitting naked-singularity boundary conditions.

status_evidence.title: Supergravity and a Bogomol'nyi Bound in Three Dimensions
status_evidence.snippet: Derives Bogomol'nyi bounds in supergravity via SUSY-based methods, focused on three dimensions.
status_evidence.claim: Demonstrates the Nester/SUSY approach to BPS bounds but does not treat 4D primary scalar hair with singular boundary conditions.
